**Provenance §4 malformed-prose policy: Actor is an all-or-nothing anchor (ruling 3b)**

What: Pinned the malformed/partial §4-prose behavior of parseProvenance (design.md Decision 6).

Policy: The **Actor line is the block ANCHOR and is all-or-nothing** — ACTOR_LINE_RE requires a well-formed `@actor (humano|agente)` pair. A kind-less Actor (`**Actor:** @x`) or an unknown kind (`(robot)`) does NOT anchor a block → parseProvenance returns every field undefined + content unchanged → the export's @legacy fallback keeps the malformed prose verbatim in content (declared, never dropped). Optional **Fuente/Supersede are best-effort, order-anchored**: recovered only if well-formed and in sequence; a malformed one ends the block and stays in content.

Why anchor-strict not lenient: a lenient parser recovering `@x` from a kind-less Actor would have to fabricate an actorKind (there is no `unknown` in the enum — the fallback's whole point is that uncertainty lives in `source`, not a guessed structured field).

Where: brain/scripts/memory/lib/provenance.mjs (parseProvenance state machine :65-103); negatives in provenance.test.mjs (kind-less, unknown-kind, valid-Actor+malformed-Fuente) + engram-export.test.mjs (malformed → @legacy, preserved verbatim). Ruling 3b of the CP-C2 re-split.

Learned: This behavior EMERGES from the fixed-order Actor-anchored state machine (BLOCKER-1 fix) — it wasn't separately designed. Characterization tests pin it (GREEN on first run, honestly noted as such — not RED→GREEN).
